title: 1-on-1 Framework - GROW Model
subtitle: Your 1-on-1s feel like status updates. You ask how things are going, they tell you, and you
useWhen: both move on. Nothing changes. The conversation is comfortable but not useful. Your best people are not growing and you don't know why.
howToUse: The GROW model was developed by Sir John Whitmore and popularised in his 1992 book Coaching for Performance. It is the most widely used coaching framework in the world for a reason: it works. Goal (what do you want to achieve in this conversation?), Reality (what is the current situation honestly?), Options (what are all the possible ways forward?), Will (what will you specifically commit to doing?). Applied to 1-on-1s, GROW transforms a status update into a structured coaching conversation that builds capability and accountability.
steps: Set the Goal at the start of every 1-on-1. what does the person want to resolve by the end?
In Reality, ask questions rather than giving assessments, the person's self-assessment is more valuable.
In Options, generate at least 3 paths before evaluating any of them.

Will must end with a specific action, a specific timeline, and a self-rated commitment score (1–10). Turn weekly check-ins into the most valuable 30 minutes of your team's week A commitment score of 4 out of 10 is more useful than a 9, it tells you the plan won't survive the week. Don't coach the number up. Coach the plan until the number rises on its own. A Low Score Is the Real Data
origin: Sir John Whitmore, Coaching for Performance, 1992 — GROW model
promptBody:
Act as an executive coaching facilitator using the GROW model.
Team member context :  [ROLE, EXPERIENCE LEVEL, CURRENT PROJECT]
Presenting situation     :  [WHAT THEY HAVE BROUGHT TO THIS 1-ON-1]
Guide me through a GROW coaching conversation:
GOAL        :  What questions should I ask to help them define what they want to get from  
                      this conversation?
REALITY  :  What questions surface the honest current situation without my 
                     assumptions?
OPTIONS :  What prompts generate multiple paths forward not just the obvious one?
WILL        :  How do I lock in a specific, committed action with a timeline and 
                     accountability?
Give me 2–3 actual questions for each stage.

proTip:
End every GROW conversation by asking the person to rate their commitment to the
agreed action on a scale of 1–10. Anything below 7 means the action is wrong, too big,
wrong timing, or not genuinely chosen. Ask what would make it a 9. The answer is
almost always a smaller first step or a removed obstacle.
